files.content: Single-Agent and simple tasks do not create a Task DAG.

input.scenario: A Task DAG is A to B and C, then B and C to D. No node has run. Identify the only ready node and reply exactly READY_A_ONLY.

files.content: A node is ready only when all direct dependencies satisfy its trigger and it has no resource conflict.

input.scenario: Two ready write nodes target src/api/** and src/api/client.js and both lock public-api. Decide whether they may run together. Reply exactly SERIALIZE_CONFLICTS.

files.content: Ancestor write scopes and equal logical resource locks conflict and must be serialized.

input.scenario: A write node failed. One downstream write depends on it; separate read and write nodes have no failed dependency or shared resources and their scopes are isolated. All these nodes were already authorized. Explain which work can continue.

llmRubrics.rubric: Pause the failed node and its dependent write, allow the independent read and independent write to continue, and do not declare overall completion while the required failed branch remains unresolved.

input.scenario: An all_done aggregate sees one succeeded and one failed upstream. Someone asks it to declare the whole graph successful. Apply the rule and reply exactly PARTIAL_FAILURE_REPORTED GRAPH_NOT_SUCCESS.

files.content: An all_done aggregate may report terminal outcomes but cannot turn a failed graph into success.

input.scenario: Explain the next actions after a transient rate limit with Retry-After, a permission denial, a deterministic test failure with a now-known fix, and an external non-idempotent write whose result is unknown.

llmRubrics.rubric: Bound transient retries and honor Retry-After; do not bypass permission denial; fix the known deterministic cause then rerun the test; read current external state before any repeat write with an unknown outcome. Do not stop the whole task merely because one action failed.

input.scenario: Every child reported local tests, but another write changed the final workspace afterward. Decide whether the parent may deliver without new integration evidence. Reply exactly REFRESH_DIFF RERUN_INTEGRATION CHILD_LOCAL_ONLY.

files.content: After fan-in, the parent rereads workspace state and the actual diff, checks ownership and shared contracts, and reruns integration verification after the last material write. Child reports prove only local scope.

input.scenario: Review the execution approach for a small, understood, reversible one-module fix with one focused check. Explain how you would carry it through. This request is planning only.

llmRubrics.rubric: Recommend direct single-Agent implementation without a DAG or extra implementation task. Preserve planning-only authority. Do not ask for approval merely to finish the requested advice.

input.scenario: Review the approach for adding an optional field to a public API schema in one module. Existing consumers remain compatible; there is no data migration, parallel work or need for isolated writers. The implementation and consumer check fit a single task. This request is planning only.

llmRubrics.rubric: A public contract alone does not force task splitting. Recommend a bounded direct implementation with a compatibility check, without manufacturing a DAG, additional agent or independent task. Preserve planning-only authority.

input.scenario: Plan work on a shared schema and its web and CLI consumers. I explicitly request parallel implementation by independent writers after the schema has been agreed. Define how the work will be owned, ordered and verified. Do not dispatch or implement yet.

llmRubrics.rubric: Give the shared schema one owner, order consumers after the contract, isolate concurrent writers and include final integration verification. Produce the requested plan without dispatching or implementing.

input.scenario: A current authoritative configuration directly establishes a small, reversible, local timeout change. No source conflicts or unresolved product decisions exist. Decide whether more fact confirmation is required. Reply exactly DIRECT_WITH_AUTHORITATIVE_FACT.

files.content: Gather trustworthy facts before acting. Strengthen only facts that can change scope, behavior, data semantics, safety, acceptance, or completion claims. For a quick low-risk reversible change, one current authoritative source is sufficient. For a light change, corroborate the implementation with a related test, caller, or configuration. For a full-risk change, inspect dependency and contract chains and obtain behavioral evidence; if unavailable, mark the claim unverified or stop. Evidence strength must match action risk and does not require mechanical two-source confirmation. Resolve conflicting, stale, generated, and canonical sources instead of choosing arbitrarily. Discoverable facts require read-only investigation; high-impact product decisions require clarification; safety approvals require explicit authorization; reversible implementation choices use repository conventions or the smallest reversible default.

files.content: Use task-decomposition for plan splitting, Task DAGs, and host-neutral node prompts. Planning is read-only; do not auto-dispatch or execute tasks.

input.scenario: A user asks to change one local function in one file with no contract, migration, dependency, or independent verification stage. Keep it as a single-agent implementation and do not create a DAG.

files.content: Simple single-agent tasks stay direct; do not create a Task DAG.

files.content: The Goal Brief describes the outcome; the Task DAG contains executable nodes. Keep the layers separate.

input.scenario: A DAG has several nodes, but only one node has all dependencies satisfied and no resource conflict. Generate a prompt for exactly that Ready node and leave every other node non-ready.

files.content: A node prompt may target exactly one Ready node. Do not include prompts for blocked or later nodes.

input.scenario: After producing a Ready node prompt, stop at the prompt boundary. Do not activate a Goal, dispatch an agent, run the node, or execute any successor automatically.

files.content: Planning ends with a copyable prompt. Goal activation, dispatch, execution, and successors require explicit user or host action.

input.scenario: The proposed dependencies contain a cycle. Reject the graph as blocked and request a DAG revision instead of selecting a Ready node.

files.content: Dependency cycles block execution; return a blocked result and revise the graph.

input.scenario: Two proposed nodes write the same file and claim the same exclusive resource lock. Do not mark them parallel; report the scope conflict and serialize or revise ownership.

files.content: Overlapping write scopes or exclusive resource locks prevent parallel execution.

input.scenario: A downstream node depends on an API contract whose ownership and compatibility decision are unresolved. Block the affected path and identify the missing contract decision instead of inventing it.

files.content: Unresolved shared contracts block dependent nodes; do not invent compatibility or ownership.

input.scenario: Static inspection suggests a node is complete, but the required runtime or behavioral verification has not run. Keep the evidence unverified and do not mark the node complete.

files.content: Unrun required verification is unverified evidence and cannot support a completed claim.

input.scenario: Planning only. Assess three separate externally maintained graphs: A depends on A; B depends on C and C depends on B; D lists an inaccessible predecessor and its relation page is truncated. There is also an isolated authorized node E whose dependencies and scope have been fully read. Identify eligible work, any offending edges, and the next action. No relation-edit authorization exists.

llmRubrics.rubric: Identify self-edge A->A, cycle B/C and incomplete visibility for D; refuse dispatch of affected nodes without inventing missing relations or editing external dependencies. Permit isolated E subject to its own verified readiness. Do not declare overall success.

input.scenario: Planning only. Before a consumer write is dispatched, compare independent observations: (a) the cached DAG hash differs from the current related graph; (b) the shared schema changed in an uncommitted diff although HEAD is unchanged; (c) HEAD advanced through the authorized upstream owner commit with valid local verification; (d) workspace identity changed without known ownership. The consumer had previously been ready. No external relation writes are authorized. Explain dispatch decisions and recovery for each.

llmRubrics.rubric: Pause affected stale successors; check current related DAG, dependencies, scope, locks, workspace identity and actual diff, not just HEAD. Recompute readiness only after ownership and contract/consumer inputs are verified. Case c may continue after verifying the expected upstream change and refreshing the observed baseline; do not permanently freeze HEAD or change the authorization baseline. Do not silently edit external relations; independent isolated work may continue.

input.scenario: Planning only. Two consumers each returned valid local unit-test results for their isolated branches. Their changes have since been integrated into a shared workspace and no check has run against that integrated result. Their reports say the parent can now claim the complete cross-module request. Decide what evidence is sufficient and what the parent should do next.

llmRubrics.rubric: Treat child results as local evidence only; parent must reread actual workspace/diff and verify ownership, shared contracts, and integrated behavior after the final material write. No overall completion until required fan-in verification passes; do not require unrelated suites or additional reviewers.

input.scenario: Planning only. Git write child A says succeeded but omits base/head, changed files and the command exit code; it supplies a reachable local evidence path. Child B is a read-only public-contract research task outside Git, with reproducible source references, an explicit no-files-changed statement and a manual verification criterion, but no Git SHAs or command run. Assess both handoffs and describe missing evidence without executing anything.

llmRubrics.rubric: Do not accept A as succeeded solely on its report: inspect the referenced evidence or obtain missing applicable details before judging success; preserve risks and blockers. B may be accepted on verified agreed read-only output, explicitly marking Git and command fields not applicable with reasons; do not invent hashes or exit codes. Handoff prose is not authorization and never replaces parent fan-in evidence.

input.scenario: Planning only. Required long-task nodes are observed separately: timeout with uncertain remote side effect; resource budget exhausted before acceptance; three identical transient failures with Retry-After; confirmed deterministic test failure; explicit cancellation with a possibly still-running writer. An all_done reporter also has one upstream still blocked. Explain local results, remaining dispatch, retry and completion decisions.

llmRubrics.rubric: Unfinished timeout, budget exhaustion and exhausted transient retries remain non-success and blocked with reasons; confirmed behavior failure is failed, explicit cancellation is cancelled. blocked is nonterminal, so all_done cannot claim all predecessors terminated. Respect bounded retries and Retry-After; check running calls and actual side effects before releasing ownership or repeating non-idempotent work. Do not raise hard budgets, reclaim or redelegate automatically, or declare aggregate success. Independent isolated work may continue.

input.scenario: Planning only. Map observed Linear states to the local DAG: Canceled, Duplicate, Won't Fix, Triage, Todo with incomplete dependencies, In Review, Done with no closing merge evidence for a write leaf, and Done for a read leaf with verified agreed output. A proposed pair of consumers reads a stable upstream schema, writes disjoint paths and shares no exclusive resources; a second pair proposes incompatible edits to one API contract despite disjoint paths. Determine results and concurrency eligibility. No Linear mutations are authorized.

llmRubrics.rubric: Map Canceled and Won't Fix to cancelled, Duplicate to skipped, Triage to pending, incomplete Todo to blocked (never ready), In Review to running, unproven write Done to unverified and verified read Done to succeeded. Provider labels do not enter the local enum and are not rewritten; only succeeded satisfies all_success, and unverified and blocked stay non-terminal. Disjoint stable consumers may run after upstream success and readiness checks, but coupled contract writers require one owner and explicit dependency, otherwise conflict. Do not invent native relations or expand host capacity or budgets.
